**Starts** once #60 and #57 are merged.

## Why

Option cards let the user choose among a stop's or stay's candidates with a click, instead of only in chat (functional spec 7.5). The card actions also ask for more options or a different budget tier.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 7.1, 7.5, and 7.6.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (refine), 7.2, and 9.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3.9.

## Open questions

- ~~Which attractions show a rating and review count? A national park or a historic plaque shows none (functional spec 7.5).~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** every place shows its rating and review count when Google has one, attractions included, and nothing when it has none. Hiding them would take a list of Google place types, such as `national_park` and `historical_landmark`, and Google has dozens of attraction types, with edge cases such as a state park or a scenic overlook. A rating on a park does no harm, and the review count shows when a rating is thin, such as "5.0 stars, 3 reviews". Write it into functional spec 7.5, in place of "Attractions show them only where a rating means something…", and into Google design 2.2's "Rating and review count" row.
- ~~Do Google's terms require the "Summarized with Gemini" label wherever a Places summary appears?~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** no label, since the app never shows a Places summary to the user. Summaries go only to the workers, in search results, and the card shows the worker's own rationale and notes (functional spec 7.5). Google's [Places API policies](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/policies) apply when a summary is shown: its full text, unchanged, with Google's disclosure text just below it, an "About this summary" link, and a "Report summary" link. A review summary also needs a "Review summary" heading and a "See reviews" link. Write into Google design 2.2 that any screen that ever shows a Places summary follows those rules.

  The same page has two rules that do apply to the cards, since they show Google's name, type, rating, and review count away from the Google map. Places data shown without a Google map needs Google Maps attribution, the Google Maps logo, or the text "Google Maps" where space is short, always visible and never changed. Google says to put it "near the top or bottom of the content, and within the same visual container", so a page footer doesn't count, but one logo can cover every card in one panel. A card that stands alone, such as one in the chat, needs its own. And Google's content, such as the rating, must be set apart from ours, such as the rationale. Write both rules into Google design 2.2, not a fixed layout, since the layout may change in #204.

## Do

- Show an option card for the newest candidate set of each stop and stay with nothing selected, with each candidate's details. Select, More options, Higher tier, and Lower tier each send a message to the coordinator.
- Show no card for new options on a stop or stay that already has a pick. Functional spec 7.5 says one opens, and goes away on a reload. That's fiddly screen code: the browser would have to notice the new set and forget it on a reload. A rule on saved data, such as "the newest set is newer than the pick's", would come back after a reload, and stay open when the user picks from an older set in chat. Instead, the coordinator names the new options in chat, and the user picks there. Change functional spec 7.5 to match. Add a line to the coordinator's instructions: when the stop or stay already has a pick, there's no card, so name the new options in chat, and say which one you'd recommend. Decided on 2026-10-28 in chat, as a start: how the cards look isn't settled yet, so it may change once they're built.
- Show one Google Maps attribution in each container that shows option cards, and set Google's content, such as the rating, apart from ours, such as the rationale (Google design 2.2, from the settled question above).
- Add the coordinator's instructions for card actions. "Higher tier" and "Lower tier" are requests, such as "something nicer than these", sent to a worker. Nothing is stored (technical spec section 9).
- Fix technical spec section 9's "Higher tier" and "Lower tier" bullet to match 5.2: sending a worker for them takes no read, since the worker reads the candidates already offered itself, with `read_worker_brief_facts` (#191). Section 9 still says "The coordinator reads the stop or stay, and sends a worker." Changed on 2026-10-28, in place of an older item from #129 that asked for the read.
- Add the end of technical spec 5.2's bullet "When the user turns down a place", which #56 left out since it needs option cards and workers. #56's "Rejecting places" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` has a first bullet that ends "whether or not it's selected." Add after it, word for word: "The card then shows what's left, so a worker is needed only when no candidates are left or the user asks for more options." Added on 2026-10-26, from #56.

## Done when

On the deployed site (systems design, section 7), on the Moab trip (domain model, section 5.2):

- Each stop and stay with candidates and nothing selected shows a card with its newest set. Each option shows its tier where it has one, and its rating and review count where Google has one. No option shows a price.
- "Higher tier" is hidden on a card where every option is upscale, and "Lower tier" on one where every option is value.
- Each container with cards shows the Google Maps attribution.
- "Higher tier" then Select updates the itinerary, and the coordinator confirms in chat (functional spec 11, S6).

What the workers pick for S5 (functional spec 11) is checked in #60, and the whole scenario in #69. Changed on 2026-10-28, since #184 made tiers labels and dropped the budget rule.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-29-option-cards).
